newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, consolidation seen.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end nearly flat, consolidation seen.

text.p: Stocks closed nearly flat on Saturday as an early momentum focused on small-sized shares lost steam over economic woes, brokers said.
The composite index ended 0.71 point higher at 782.13.
"Profit-taking set in after a rebound," said Kim Heung-shik of Hyundai Securities. "Further consolidation is likely on Monday over fears of an economic slump."
Brokers said the index would test the 760 line next week.
Volume totalled 13.76 million shares for Saturday's half-day trading, compared with 21.39 million on Friday.
Gainers outpaced losers 409 to 379 with 102 unchanged.
Brokers said tightening liquidity ahead of the Korean Thanksgiving holidays in September was a depressing element.
"Pessimism about the market's future was so strong as to swamp the government's boosting measures this week," said Yoo Jae-kyong of Daishin Securities.

On Thursday, the finance ministry revealed a reform programme designed to streamline the securities industry, including allowing margin trading in second-tier stocks. It said on Friday it would raise the paid-up capital of the Korea Europe Fund by 50 percent to $240 million in October.
